name: his_own_older_statement_against_a_document
why: The rubric's hard case and the owner's own starting rule: his own words beat a document even when the document is newer. A miss here means the pack reads freshness as the first rule instead of the second.

pairs.subject: the flagging threshold for the tide gauges

first.text: Use 0.55 for flagging on the gauges, not 0.7. I looked at the misses and 0.7 is too slack.

second.text: The flagging threshold is 0.70. Readings at or above it are flagged for review.

name: two_of_the_same_standing_the_later_wins
why: The second rule standing alone: two sources the model wrote, so freshness is the only rule in play and the later must win.

pairs.subject: where the gauge pipeline writes its day files

first.text: The pipeline writes its day files under the scratch directory and clears them each night.

second.text: The pipeline writes its day files under the archive directory and keeps them for a season.

name: the_same_shape_about_different_work_is_no_conflict
why: The commonest false positive, and the reason `disagree` is asked first: two thresholds, two pieces of work, no disagreement. A pack that answered 'which wins' for this pair would be answering a question that was never asked.

second.text: The ferry alarm sounds at 0.80 of capacity.

name: two_stages_of_one_plan_both_happened
why: A difference in time is not a disagreement when both were true at their own stage. A miss here would make every record of a change read as a conflict with the record before it.

first.text: For the first season let us run the pipeline by hand after each spring tide.

second.text: The pipeline has run on a timer since the summer, as we planned it would once it was steady.

name: more_detail_is_not_disagreement
why: One source says less than the other and nothing against it. A reader can hold both, so there is nothing to choose between them.

first.text: The gauges report regularly through the day.

second.text: The gauges report every ten minutes, and twice that often during a spring tide.

name: a_document_recording_him_changing_his_mind
why: The rubric's one exception: the later source carries his voice, so it wins against his own earlier words. This is the case the exception clause exists for, and the one a rubric of two bare rules gets wrong.

pairs.subject: the flagging threshold for the tide gauges

first.text: Use 0.55 for flagging on the gauges.

second.text: Decision note, written down from what the owner said on the call: he has changed his mind about the gauge threshold and wants 0.70 from now on.

name: a_quote_does_not_outrank_what_it_quotes
why: A source that only repeats another is not a statement of its own. A miss here lets a summary of his words outrank the words, and then a chain of summaries outranks everything.

first.text: Earlier in this conversation it was said that nobody reviews the gauge reports before they go out.

second.text: I read every gauge report myself before it goes out.

name: outside_text_against_his_own_words
why: Text from outside the harness has the least standing of all, and it is the one place where getting precedence wrong lets a page overwrite what he said.

pairs.subject: the gauge library's supported reading rate

first.text: We read the gauges every ten minutes and that is what our licence covers.

second.text: Fetched page: the library supports reading every thirty seconds and recommends it for all users.

name: one_value_against_another_for_the_same_setting
why: The plainest conflict there is, with both rules pointing the same way: his own words, and the later of the two. If this one misses, nothing else in the set means anything.

pairs.subject: how long the archive keeps a day file

first.text: Keep a day file for ninety days and then let it go.

second.text: Day files are kept for one year.

name: a_conflict_and_a_non_conflict_in_one_request
why: Two pairs in one request, each asked on its own: the pack must not let one pair's answer colour the other's, which is what a per-item Noul is for.

pairs.subject: the flagging threshold for the tide gauges

first.text: Flag a gauge reading at 0.55, and do not change it again without asking me.

pairs.subject: the gauges, and the ferry timetable

first.text: The gauges report every ten minutes.

second.text: The ferry sails on the hour between April and October.
